In [[knot theory]], the '''three-twist knot''' is the [[twist knot]] with three-half twists. It is listed as the '''5<sub>2</sub> knot'''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pinsky |first1=Tali |title=On the topology of the Lorenz system |url=http://rspa.royalsocietypublishing.org/content/473/2205/20170374.figures-only#F8 |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences |volume=473 |issue=2205 |publisher=The Royal Society |access-date=26 August 2018 |article-number=20170374 |language=en |doi=10.1098/rspa.2017.0374 |pmid=28989313 |pmc=5627380 |date=1 September 2017 |quote=(b) the knot with three half-twists, called the 52 knot.}}</ref> in the [[Alexander-Briggs notation]], and is one of two knots with [[crossing number (knot theory)|crossing number]] five, the other being the [[cinquefoil knot]].

The 5<sub>2</sub> knot can be represented with the following [[parametric equation]]: <ref name="t523">{{cite journal | last1=Boocher | first1=Adam | last2=Daigle | first2=Jay | last3=Hoste | first3=Jim | last4=Zheng | first4=Wenjing | title=Sampling Lissajous and Fourier Knots | journal=Experimental Mathematics | volume=18 | issue=4 | date=2009 | issn=1058-6458 | doi=10.1080/10586458.2009.10129057 | pages=481–497 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10586458.2009.10129057 | access-date=2026-07-26| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

:<math>\begin{align}
  x &=  \cos(2\phi) \\
  y &=  \cos(5\phi + \pi/4) \\
  z &=  \cos(2\phi + \pi/2) + \cos(3\phi + \pi/4)
\end{align}</math>

with <math>0\leq\phi\leq 2\pi</math>.

==Properties==
The three-twist knot is a [[prime knot]], and it is [[invertible knot|invertible]] but not [[amphichiral knot|amphichiral]].  Its [[Alexander polynomial]] is

:<math>\Delta(t) = 2t-3+2t^{-1}, \,</math>

since <math>\begin{pmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{pmatrix}</math> is a possible [[Seifert surface|Seifert matrix]], or because of its [[Alexander polynomial#Alexander–Conway polynomial|Conway polynomial]], which is

:<math>\nabla(z) = 2z^2+1, \, </math>

and its [[Jones polynomial]] is

:<math>V(q) = q^{-1} - q^{-2} + 2q^{-3} - q^{-4} + q^{-5} - q^{-6}. \, </math><ref>{{Knot Atlas|5_2}}</ref>

Because the Alexander polynomial is not [[monic polynomial|monic]], the three-twist knot is not [[fibered knot|fibered]].

The three-twist knot is a [[hyperbolic knot]], with its complement having a [[Hyperbolic volume (knot)|volume]] of approximately 2.82812.

If the fibre of the knot in the initial image of this page were cut at the bottom right of the image, and the ends were pulled apart, it would result in a single-stranded [[Figure-of-nine loop#Figure-of-nine knot|figure-of-nine knot]] (not the figure-of-nine loop).
